The '''2019–20 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team''' represented [[Purdue University]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]] in his 15th season with the Boilers. The team played their home games at [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Boilers finished the season 16–15, 9–11 in [[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for 10th place. Due to tie-breaking rules, they received the No. 10 seed in the [[2020 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] before the tournament was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2020-big-ten-tournament-canceled-thursday-amid-coronavirus-pandemic-concerns/live/|title=2020 Big Ten tournament canceled Thursday amid coronavirus pandemic concerns|website=CBSSports.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-13}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2018–19 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Boilermakers]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 26–10, 16–4 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to win a share of the Big Ten regular season championship, the school's conference-record 24th championship. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they were upset by [[2018–19 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401120735|title=Minnesota vs. Purdue - Game Summary - March 15, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> The received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 3 seed in the South region. They defeated [[2018–19 Old Dominion Monarchs basketball team|Old Dominion]] in the First Round<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123399|title=Old Dominion vs. Purdue - Game Recap - March 21, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> before beating defending champion [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123432|title=Villanova vs. Purdue - Game Recap - March 23, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> In the Sweet Sixteen, they defeated [[2018–19 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in overtime to advance to the Elite Eight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/03/28/tennessee-vols-basketball-purdue-ncaa-tournament-rick-barnes/3263933002/|title=Tennessee basketball races back against Purdue, then falls in overtime in Sweet 16|website=Knoxville News Sentinel|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31|archive-date=2019-03-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329140832/https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/03/28/tennessee-vols-basketball-purdue-ncaa-tournament-rick-barnes/3263933002/|url-status=dead}}</ref> There they lost to No. 1 seed [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in overtime.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/31/sports/ncaa-tournament-virginia-purdue.html|title=Virginia Fends Off Purdue and Naysayers to Reach the Final Four|last=Depaolo|first=Joe|date=2019-03-31|work=The New York Times|access-date=2019-03-31|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

==Offseason==

===Coaching changes===
In March 2019, assistant [[Greg Gary (basketball)|Greg Gary]] was hired as the new head coach at [[Mercer Bears men's basketball|Mercer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.coachesdatabase.com/greg-gary-hired-mercer/|title=Purdue assistant Greg Gary named head coach at Mercer|website=coachesdatabase.com|publisher=Coaches Database|date=March 26, 2019|accessdate=November 5, 2019}}</ref> As a result, Painter hired [[Micah Shrewsberry]] to return as associate head coach in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/05/08/micah-shrewsberry-returning-purdue-basketball-assistant-coach/1148466001/|title=Purdue basketball bringing back Micah Shrewsberry as assistant coach|publisher=Lafayette Journal & Courier|date=May 8, 2019|accessdate=November 5, 2019}}</ref>
